about: Local building habits, as rules on what each building is. Read by tools/character (see the top of its __init__.py for how a rule is written). A map can add to or change these with tools/character/maps/<map>.json.

styles.about: The years a style name means, earliest and latest. They date a building that OpenStreetMap names a style (building:architecture) and, where the data says nothing of a building's age, the zones of tools/area.py that carry a style's name.

evidence.about: How far each source is trusted to date a building, best first. A listed building is dated as built before listed_before: Historic England lists nearly everything standing from before 1840 and very little from after the First World War, so it is a fair guess where the certificates and the mappers say nothing.

area_railings.about: Railings along the top of the retaining wall where steps drop beside the pavement into a sunken area in front of a house.
area_railings.asks: thing: the flight, with front_gap, the metres between the pavement's edge and the house's front wall. building: the nearest building's character.

rules.name: town house area
rules.why: The urban terraced town house, built from the late 1600s to about 1914 (Georgian, Regency and much of Victorian, in London, Bristol, Edinburgh, Dublin and Bath alike), has a basement or semi-basement and a raised ground floor, with an open area between it and the pavement fenced with iron railings. Small workers' cottages and later houses rarely do.
